latin: Lūsitānia, Lūsitāniae f. · Lisbōna, Lisbōnae f.
keywords: fābulae fabulae Theodōrus et pater Place names: Portugal / Lisbon / Coimbra / Sintra / Portuguese Lūsitānia, Lūsitāniae f. · Lisbōna, Lisbōnae f. Ancient names Post-classical names Quantity notes Lūsitānia, Lūsitāniae f. — Portugal; the ancient name of the province (L&S). Lūsitānus, Lūsitāna, Lūsitānum — Portuguese; Lūsitānicē — in Portuguese, our adverb, formed like Latīnē . Lisbōna, Lisbōnae f. — Lisbon, the form used in the fābulae (Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates orbis terrarum I, 1572, “vulgo Lisbona”); the ō follows Olisīpōn- . Olisīpō, Olisīpōnis m. — the ancient name (Pliny, NH 4.117; L&S Olisipo , with ī), for recognition. Conimbrica, Conimbricae f. — Coimbra, a post-classical transfer of the name; Conimbriga, Conimbrigae f. — the Roman town nearby (Pliny 4.113 prints Conimbrica ); Aeminium, Aeminiī n. — Roman Coimbra itself. Stem quantities are not established and are left unmarked. Sintra, Sintrae f. — Sintra, the modern name declined in Latin (medieval Sintria ; ancient Mōns Lūnae ). Antanhol — the grandparents’ village, indeclinable. Tagus, Tagī m. — the Tagus (L&S); Portus Cale — Porto; Alfama — indeclinable; statiō Orientālis — Gare do Oriente; Hortī Nātiōnum — Parque das Nações. obrigado / obrigada — Portuguese “thank you”, from Latin obligātus, obligāta , “obliged”; the form agrees with the speaker. Cities and small places take no preposition: Lisbōnam volābimus , Lisbōnae sumus , Sintrā (from Sintra); countries take one: in Lūsitāniam , in Lūsitāniā . Ubi est Lūsitānia? Longēne abest? — Where is Portugal? Is it far away? (Fābula I, Iter in Lūsitāniam ). Sintram īmus. — We’re going to Sintra. (Fābula I, Iter in Lūsitāniam ). Scīsne, Theodōre, quid sit obrigado? Lūsitānī ita grātiās agunt. — Do you know, Theo, what obrigado is? That’s how the Portuguese say thank you. (Fābula IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis ). The quantity of Lisbōna follows the fābulae and lexicon-notes-01; Conimbrica, Conimbriga and Serdica are left unmarked because their quantities are not established in the checked sources.
